title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_5af
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy Fysbis backdoor compromise in a target network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. The Fysbis malware is a modular Linux trojan/backdoor that implements plug-in and controller modules as distinct classes. It includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of Executable and Linking Format (ELF) binaries. The malware can install itself on a victim system with or without root privileges, providing flexibility for adversaries in selecting accounts for installation. It has capabilities for remote shell access, persistence, and command and control (C2) communication.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any connected hosts. Enter `start` to proceed.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any connected hosts. Enter `start` to proceed.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Connections
levels.content: While monitoring the `target` host, you notice unusual outbound network connections. Identify the suspicious network port used for these connections.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious network port, you can use the `netstat` or `ss` command to list all active network connections. Look for any unusual ports that are not part of standard services. The suspicious port used for these connections is `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and look for any unusual ports.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `netstat` or `ss` command to list all active network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious port is not a standard service port. Focus on ports that are typically not used by legitimate services.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot on the `target` host.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, investigate systemd services and timers. The suspicious service is automatically started using a systemd service named `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service name is unusual and does not match standard system services. Focus on services that seem out of place.

levels.title: Collect Forensic Evidence
levels.content: Gather forensic evidence supporting the identified malicious activity on the `target` host. This includes relevant logs, process information, service configuration, and network evidence.
levels.solution: To collect forensic evidence, look for logs in `/var/log/` and check running processes. The relevant logs and process information can be found in `/var/log/local-inventory/inventory.log` and the running processes can be checked using the `ps` command.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for logs in `/var/log/` and check running processes.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the logs in `/var/log/local-inventory/inventory.log` and the running processes using the `ps` command.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The logs contain detailed information about the malicious activity. Focus on logs that are not part of standard system logs.
